blocks.text: Mendoza: cultivated fields and trees beneath snow-capped peaks
The Andes and the Mendoza area

After breakfast, you’ll set off for a full day in the mountains.

The drive follows an international highway through the foothills of the Andes. Your first stop is Uspallata, a high-altitude town surrounded by mountains, where old buildings and structures still stand.

The route then takes you past the Picheuta Bridge and the Los Penitentes ski resort. You’ll see the thermal waters at Puente del Inca before continuing to Aconcagua Park.

In the park, you’ll walk along the trails and have time to take photos with the Andes as a backdrop. The last stop is Las Cuevas, a village about 3,500 m above sea level, where you can get a feel for life high in the Andes.

In the evening, you’ll return to your hotel in Mendoza.
Mendoza skyline with a green dome, high-rise buildings and distant mountains, Argentina
Mendoza: city rooftops and mountains on the horizon

After breakfast, you’ll set out on a wine tour.

The Uco Valley lies in the foothills of the Andes and is one of Mendoza’s main wine regions. You’ll head there in the morning with a guide who specialises in wine.

You’ll visit three well-known wineries. Malbec is the region’s main grape variety. Your guide will explain how grapes are grown and harvested, how wine is made and what happens at each stage of ageing.

Part of the tour focuses on tasting, including how to hold your glass, taste the wine and pair it with food. You’ll have lunch at one of the wineries.

You’ll then visit the church of Our Lady of Carrodilla, who is regarded as the patron saint of vineyards.

The tour lasts about half a day.

**Meals:** breakfast.
